name: WXC sell hook burns the sold amount from the pair before pricing the sale
summary: On a sell, WXC's transfer hook burns the net amount being sold from the WXC/WBNB pair's balance and calls sync() before the sold tokens arrive, so the sale is priced against a reserve already reduced by its own size. Inside a Moolah WBNB flash loan the attacker bought 74.96M WXC (about half the reserve) for 49.15 WBNB and sold it straight back: the hook burned 70.47M WXC from the pair, leaving 0.2M, and the sale returned 86.70 WBNB.
notes: The reset is the upgrade to implementation 0x4c100d30 about an hour before the exploit. Earlier implementations already burned on sells, but every one of the 19 pre-exploit pair burns since the proxy's deployment was an ordinary sell of at most 6,601 WXC, so none was an earlier exploit.
Campaign: three buy-and-sell round trips by 0x888a8dfe through contract 0xdc2a7aad two hours later against the drained pair. Later sells through 0x00000047 are ordinary sells.
Loss is the pair's net WBNB depletion, which includes 4.35 WBNB the hook's own fee swap paid to the fee recipient within the anchor; burned WXC is not valued: the attacker realised nothing from it.
